results.title: A transaction with one invalid command changes nothing and names that command
Each changing transaction adds one revision; a transaction that changes nothing adds none
Undo and redo add revisions; a new edit after undo drops the redo branch without reusing ids
An edit or undo based on an older revision is refused and changes nothing
Deleting an atom deletes exactly the bonds that touch it
Repeating a completed edit with the same request_id and body returns the first reply without applying it again
Reusing a request_id for a different request is refused and changes nothing
Saved title, atoms (element, charge, isotope, position), bonds and history survive a crash
Edits that were neither saved nor drafted are gone after a crash; the last save remains
Unsaved work in a recovery draft survives a crash and is recovered with its history
Charge, isotope, coordinate, element and request_id just outside their ranges are refused and change nothing; the range ends are accepted
Closing with unsaved changes is refused unless the client confirms the revision it discards
Capabilities name bounded formats and valence while unimplemented features stay explicit
Formula and isotope masses use one unchanged graph and a pinned synthetic public-reference fixture
A C–O drawing is written as MOL, imported into another document, and survives reopening
Chemical graph and scene positions are kept and compared separately: a second scene instance of the same graph moves independently, chemistry and the first instance stay, and undo restores each step
Group sibling graphics, move a group and child once, and restore selection through undo, redo, save and reopen
A surviving object's reference prevents target deletion until detached, and undo restores both

With two scene instances, an atom added with one position, positions that leave out an instance, an atom move that names no instance, and deleting the last instance are refused with the command index and change nothing
Stated, unknown and inferred hydrogens are told apart through edits, undo, a save and a restart (that an inferred state has no count field is checked in crates/application/tests/states.rs)
Radicals, query atoms and bonds, aromatic, dative and unknown bonds, and attachment points survive edits, element-query conversion, undo, redo, a save and a restart
Invalid combinations of recorded states are refused with their command index and reason code and change nothing
Operation contract 1 runs create, edit, save and read with a typed reply naming its contract, profile, outcome, revision, model and losses
A failed operation reports the v1 error code and facts as a diagnostic, without a result, and changes nothing
An operation that does not run, or a profile that reproduces nothing, is answered unsupported without a result or a change
A request for an operation contract version, operation or shape the service does not support is refused with a structured protocol error
Document settings are saved with the document, reopened after a crash, and undone as an edit
Preferences set the settings new documents start from and never change an existing document
Out-of-range settings, stale preference writes, and computation preferences are refused and change nothing
Valence inspection names its snapshot and does not edit it
Benzene inspection is read only; conversion is one replayable undoable edit
A Kekule pyrrole nitrogen with inferred hydrogen is pyrrole-type; conversion states its hydrogen and the Kekule form restores it to inferred
A benzene fused to a saturated ring is unsupported, never non-aromatic, and refuses conversion of the whole document

A conversion stopped by its time limit reports time_limit with only the limit, changes nothing, and is computed afresh when asked again, with another limit if wished; once completed, the same request ID with another limit is request_id_reused
Benzene identity reports its symmetric atom orbit without editing the graph
Rich CDXML preserves opaque data and projects a selected molecule only after loss consent

A CDXML fragment with WedgeBegin marks, an Or 2, an Or 258, an And 2 and an Or with no number imports the marks, one derived configuration per center and four separate groups (258 stays 258 and Or 2 stays apart from And 2), survives reopening, and reports the hints it does not store

A bond Display outside the public list, a Geometry other than Tetrahedral, a malformed BondOrdering or group number, and a group member that is not a derived tetrahedral center are refused with their reason on preview and on create, and an attribute without a public spelling stays refused
CDX is read, exported and projected through the same operations as CDXML, with canonical base64 and consent for rounded or dropped content
Acetic acid is previewed and imported from SMILES without accepting a loss, then written as recorded and canonical SMILES
Malformed, unsupported and unconsented SMILES changes nothing and names the position and the code
A Kekule benzene query finds its twelve atom mappings in an aromatic benzene target, with source and target atom IDs, and neither drawing changes
A benzene query is refused, not answered with zero mappings, when the target has a fused partially saturated ring the aromaticity model cannot classify
Drawn stereo marks are set and cleared by command, keep their narrow end, never swap the bond's ends, and follow undo and redo
A stated configuration is stored in canonical form, saved, reopened, undone, redone, and a restatement changes nothing
One centre on [F, Cl, Br, implicit hydrogen] stored with positive and with negative parity differs only in the turn, and every restatement in another order lands on one of the two
The same alkene stated same side and opposite sides gives two snapshots that differ only in the relation; unknown is a statement and clearing is not
A drawn mark and a stated configuration are separate statements: setting or clearing one with its own command never changes the other, and those commands do not check them against each other
A stereo command that cannot hold is refused with a stable reason and the failing command's index, and the transaction changes nothing
A configuration whose bonded neighbors change is cleared and the reply says so in notes; undo restores it, and a clear the client asked for or re-set in the same transaction is not listed
A bond order change or an aromaticity conversion that would break a marked or configured bond is refused whole; with the mark removed the conversion goes through
SMILES text carries no stereo, so a drawing that holds any is exported only after consent to a digest of what is dropped, and the digest does not survive a change
A V2000 molfile writes the wedge; a configuration the marks do not show is listed and written only after the caller repeats the loss digest

A wedge drawing with an absolute group is written as V3000 with CFG=1, a STEABS collection and the chiral flag, imported into another document with its mark, configuration and group, and survives reopening

V3000 constructs this profile cannot hold (a stereo collection that lists a plain atom, a bond mark on an aromatic bond, a dangling atom, a query bond type) are refused with their reason and the document keeps its revision

Absolute, and and or groups (numbers -128, omitted, 258) are written as V3000 STEABS, STERAC and STEREL collections with the chiral flag, imported into another document with the numbers as stated, survive reopening, and a V2000 export of them still needs consent

V3000 collections that repeat a type and index, share an atom, are empty, list an atom twice or a plain atom, point at a missing atom or overflow int32 are refused with their reason and the document keeps its revision, atoms and groups
Importing a V3000 file whose or group number the document already uses keeps both as separate groups, gives the new one a free number and reports the change
Identity and substructure search never read stereo: two drawings with opposite stated turns match, and the reply says stereo was not compared and was present
A wedge and the derivation sent in one transaction store the configuration the picture shows, restating it changes nothing, and undo and redo move the mark and the record together
The same four neighbors [F, Cl, Br, implicit hydrogen] drawn with Cl and Br exchanged give the two parities, derived from the picture and not stated

The derivation replaces the stored record of every item it processes, a configuration stated by hand and an unknown included, and writes nothing for an unmarked center or a skipped mark; undo restores the statements
The public authored two-centre drawing (one tapered hash at each centre) gives anticlockwise at both centres in the canonical orders, which is F[C@H](Cl)[C@H](Br)I
A derivation the drawing cannot support is refused with a stable reason and the failing command's index, and the transaction changes nothing
A wavy bond at a centre and a crossed double bond are derived as the explicit unknown statement, and replacing the wavy bond with a wedge replaces it with a definite configuration

chem.stereo compares the stored configuration with what each scene instance draws without editing: it agrees, disagrees after an atom is moved, is per instance, and reports an unmarked drawing as only stored; chem.validate has no stereo diagnostics

chem.stereo reports a marked center nothing is stored for as only drawn, two marks that conflict as not derivable with the reason, a stored hydrogen against a drawn lone pair as agreeing with label_differs, and a wedge whose narrow end is a terminal atom; it stores nothing
A CIP label is derived from a stored configuration and kept apart from the drawn marks
The same four neighbors stored with the turn reversed give the other descriptor, and the drawn wedge never moves a label
A double bond stored relatively is E or Z by the higher substituent at each end, and a bond with two equal substituents at an end is not stereogenic
A center whose ligands differ only by mass number is labeled by Rule 2 and is not stereogenic once the isotope is removed
The same molecule inserted in another atom order, or stored with the neighbors listed in another order, gives the same descriptor for the same atom
Meso-tartaric acid has one R and one S center, the natural acid two R, and a stored center with two equal ligands is not stereogenic

Ring ligands are ranked through ring-closure duplicates: the cis-1,2-dimethylcyclohexane is the meso form with one R and one S center, the trans one is chiral with two equal descriptors, and cyclohexanol C1 has two tied arms
A stored unknown is unknown, a stereogenic unit with nothing stored is listed as unspecified only on request, and a named unit is always evaluated
A ligand double bond whose geometry is not stated makes Rule 3 ambiguous: the item has no descriptor, the outcome is partial and the other items are still labeled
Centers the model cannot decide are unsupported with their reason, never none or a guess, and the other items of the same reply are still labeled
Each reason the operation can give for an item it will not label is reached by a molecule of its own, with the item unsupported or ambiguous and a loss entry naming the reason

Bad identifiers, scopes and lists are refused with the path of the first fault, a request over the node limit is refused whole with the numbers, and one atom over the item limit is unsupported, not none
Asking for labels changes nothing a document holds: not the revision, the undo and redo depth or the unsaved state, whatever edits come before and after, and a repeated request id is computed again
Centers whose descriptor is stated by their public name or by a published SMILES fixture are labeled as stated

Absolute, and and or groups are created over stored centers and read back with their stored number, interpreted number and label; renumbering and deleting a group change only that, and undo brings the group back under its identifier
The wedge column of a V2000 molfile is read into the stored mark and the configuration it shows; a stereo value no mark can carry is refused

A group number is stored exactly as stated (0, negative, omitted, the 32-bit bounds); an omitted number reads as 0 and so collides with an explicit 0 of the same kind, in either order, and a number outside 32 bits is refused
Or 1 and And 1 are two groups; the same kind with the same number is refused and points to merging; a kind change onto a taken number is refused
An absolute group and an and group coexist and a one-member group is legal; a second absolute group, an absolute group with a number and a member that is not a stored center are refused

Splitting, merging, removing members from and deleting a group, and changing an and or or group to another kind, report what is no longer stated or was not stated before; renumbering and adding members report nothing; the reply is partial exactly when it carries a note

A member that is no longer a stored center leaves its group with a note, whether its configuration is cleared by the client, marked unknown, lost with a neighbor change or lost with the atom, and a group left without members disappears; undo brings the members back
Groups follow undo and redo with their identifiers, a group created by a split keeps its identifier through undo and redo, and an identifier that was issued is not issued again
Groups, their stored numbers and their identifiers are saved and read back after a restart, and undo after the restart still removes them
Every group refusal names its reason and the failing command and changes nothing, and a command with a missing or unknown key or a wrong value does not read

Groups are not read by chem.cip, chem.identity or chem.substructure: the same descriptors, the same equivalence and the same mappings with and without groups, and chem.stereo says that groups are not examined only when there are groups
SMILES has no enhanced stereo groups, so a drawing that holds any group, a one-member group included, is exported only after consent to the dropped groups, listed with the stereo configurations
A title change, a move and a new atom leave the groups as they were and report nothing
